title: You Didn't Ship a Bug. You Just Wrote It for a Human. - Ravi Madabhushi, Scalekit
talk_summary: Ravi Madabhushi argues that identity/auth primitives built for humans and deterministic service accounts break down for non-deterministic agents, which need their own identity, fine-grained and time-bound scopes, and full auditability of who acted on whose behalf. The talk is about securing third-party API/MCP access for customer-facing agents, not about agent orchestration or model economics.

takeaways.technique: Per-agent identity with least-privilege, time-bound scopes
takeaways.what_they_do: Give each agent its own identity and narrow, attribute/context/principal-level scopes valid only for the duration of its task, rather than broad OAuth scopes or shared service credentials.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent should have permissions for limited amount of time that they're operating in

takeaways.technique: Tool surface filtered by acting principal
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of exposing every tool the app supports and letting the agent choose, only surface tools the authorizing user/context actually permits.
takeaways.evidence_quote: They typically surface all the tools that the user has access to ... and then let the agent determine what they are can or cannot do

takeaways.technique: Full action audit trail (actor, principal, authorization)
takeaways.what_they_do: Log every agent action with who took it, on whose behalf, who authorized it, what scope, and for how long, so behavior is inspectable rather than assumed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to have absolute visibility into what your agent can do, every action that's taken in your system, who took it, on behalf of whom

takeaways.technique: Just-in-time elevation instead of standing permissions
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents start least-privileged and must request elevated scope for specific actions rather than holding broad standing access.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agents should be least privileged by default and they should be able to ask for just-in-time authorization if they want elevated scopes
